paragraphs: Your team must deliver actionable insights and build data-driven solutions across EDITED. That is the kind of problem I have been working on. For my AstraZeneca-affiliated MSc dissertation I built a tool-calling LLM agent that keeps working when its data sources fail, deployed it on AWS Lambda and checked it with a three-tier framework of ~65 automated tests. After a rate-limit evaluation moved the agent from Groq to AWS Bedrock, I used the same tests to confirm it still behaved.

I care about the parts that make AI usable: grounding answers in trusted data through deterministic lookups, hallucination guards, and fallbacks for when external APIs go down. I also wrote the project's agent evaluation, including a documented hallucination-rate analysis. At 180 Degrees Consulting I prototyped an agentic tool for a loosely defined client brief and contributed to the client's production MCP server, now in live use; senior leadership rated the engagement five stars. At the Bristol × UWE AI Hackathon I paired a deterministic matching engine with a single LLM call, answering in under 3 seconds at about £0.003 per query. As a freelance engineer I built a production RAG and agentic retrieval system with LangChain and LangGraph.
Your ad asks for data science models and pipelines, which is the work I want to do next.
Could we spend 20 minutes on how the team partners with product and engineering teams?

skills.Client Delivery & Communication: Scoping ambiguous problems with clients, stakeholder demos, working with client engineering teams, code review, transparent reporting of model limitations, root-cause analysis, technical documentation

bullets: Integrated the agent into a React front end with real-time gene alias enrichment.

Needed an agent that researchers could trust on a cancer research platform, including when its tools fail: built a tool-calling agent (LangChain, Claude Haiku 4.5 on AWS Bedrock) for three use cases (gene alias resolution, prompt-engineered explanations of a fixed scoring pipeline, validated dataset descriptions), with deterministic Ensembl and HGNC calls, deterministic hallucination guards, and circuit breakers with a 19,213-gene parquet fallback for when the external APIs are unavailable.

Diagnosed where it struggled with a three-tier, ~65-test evaluation harness (tool-level → API → live) and hallucination-rate analysis, debugging failures layer by layer, and used the same harness to validate the Groq to Bedrock migration after a rate-limit evaluation.

Built the Python data pipeline: reconciled 14 heterogeneous source datasets through identifier crosswalks so the agent used trusted data, then deployed it as a Docker image on AWS Lambda (ECR, least-privilege IAM) and documented the architecture and evaluation.
